text: A message is a block of "Key: Value" header lines ended by a blank line; without Content-Length it has no body.
notes: auth/request and command/reply frames (no Content-Length) decode as header-only frames; the next frame starts right after the blank line

text: When the header block carries Content-Length, exactly that many body bytes follow the blank line.
notes: api/response body is exactly Content-Length bytes; a stream split at any byte boundary decodes to the same frames

text: A Content-Length that is not a non-negative decimal integer leaves the frame boundary unknown; the client treats it as a protocol error and closes.
notes: chappe behaviour: Content-Length x, -5, empty or 12abc closes the connection; owner gets chappe_esl_closed, connect gets {protocol_error, Reason}

text: A frame larger than the configured max_frame_bytes is rejected and the connection closed rather than buffered.
notes: chappe behaviour: Content-Length above max_frame_bytes or an unterminated header block over it closes the connection; owner gets chappe_esl_closed

text: Replies (command/reply, api/response) arrive in command order and answer the oldest unanswered command.
notes: pending commands are a FIFO; each reply goes to the oldest caller; replies with nothing pending are counted as unsolicited

text: api/response carries the api command output as its body.
notes: api/2 returns {ok, Body} with the api/response body

text: text/event-plain carries the event as URL-encoded header lines, then an optional body sized by an inner Content-Length.
notes: plain event headers are URL-decoded; Event-Name and Unique-ID read back; inner body cut at its Content-Length

text: text/event-json carries the event as one JSON object; the body is the _body field.
notes: json event headers are the object keys; _body becomes the event body

text: text/event-xml carries the event as an XML document.
notes: chappe keeps the XML body raw (no structured decoding)

text: log/data frames carry one log line as the body with Log-Level and related headers.
notes: delivered to the controlling process as {chappe_esl_log, Conn, Headers, Body}

text: text/disconnect-notice announces the end of the session; Content-Disposition linger means the channel hung up and events continue, disconnect means the socket closes.
notes: linger notice delivered as {chappe_esl_linger, Conn}; disconnect or no disposition as {chappe_esl_disconnect, Conn}

text: text/rude-rejection is sent instead of auth/request when the ACL denies the client; the body is the reason and the socket then closes.
notes: connect returns {error, {rejected, Text}} with the trimmed body, not {error, closed}

text: On auth/request the client sends "auth <password>" and the session is usable after a command/reply +OK.
notes: the fake receives "auth ClueCon"; connect returns {ok, Conn} after +OK accepted

text: A command/reply -ERR to the auth command means the password was refused.
notes: connect returns {error, {auth_failed, ReplyText}}

text: api <command> runs the command synchronously; output starting with -ERR reports a failure.
notes: api/2 returns {ok, Body}, or {error, Text} when the body starts with -ERR (trailing newline trimmed)

text: A command whose reply does not arrive in time fails the caller without breaking reply correlation.
notes: chappe behaviour: api/3 returns {error, timeout} without exiting; the late reply keeps its FIFO slot so the next api gets its own reply

text: bgapi <command> answers +OK Job-UUID at once and later sends a BACKGROUND_JOB event with the same Job-UUID whose body is the result.
notes: bgapi/2 returns {ok, JobUuid}; bgapi_await/3 returns the BACKGROUND_JOB body matched by Job-UUID

text: On an outbound socket the client first sends "connect"; the reply carries the channel data as headers.
notes: the listener sends "connect" first; the handler gets the channel with URL-decoded headers

text: After connect the client sends "linger" so FreeSWITCH keeps the socket open after hangup and the final events arrive.
notes: sent by default right after connect; #{linger => N} sends "linger N"; #{linger => false} sends nothing; the linger reply is not given to the handler

text: event <plain|json|xml> <names> subscribes to events in the chosen format.
notes: subscribe/2 sends "event plain ...", events/3 "event json ..." and "event xml ..."; events of each format are delivered

text: filter, sendevent and sendmsg are answered by command/reply +OK on success or -ERR on failure.
notes: filter/2, sendevent/3, execute/3,4 send the command bytes (headers, blank line) and return ok on +OK, {error, Text} on -ERR

text: myevents [format] [uuid] limits the events to one channel, "nixevent <names>" removes names from the subscription and "noevents" removes every subscription.
notes: myevents/2,3, nixevent/2 and noevents/1 send the command and return ok on +OK

text: A sendmsg or sendevent with a body carries Content-Length in its headers and the body after the blank line.
notes: sendmsg/4 and sendevent/4 add Content-Length; the next command frames correctly after the body

text: A registered node is connected and authenticated by its own process, which reports connecting, up or down and reconnects after a lost connection.
notes: chappe behaviour: node_add/2 starts the node; node_status/1 and nodes/0 show the state; a dropped socket goes down then up again; node_remove/1 closes it

text: Once up, the node subscribes to HEARTBEAT, BACKGROUND_JOB, CHANNEL_CREATE and CHANNEL_HANGUP_COMPLETE in json and keeps the load each HEARTBEAT reports.
notes: chappe behaviour: sessions, max_sessions, sessions_per_sec, idle_cpu and uptime_ms read from Session-Count, Max-Sessions, Session-Per-Sec-Last (the last second; Session-Per-Sec is the remaining budget), Idle-CPU and Uptime-msec; channel events move sessions between heartbeats

text: A node that sends no HEARTBEAT for twice the configured heartbeat interval is marked down and its connection closed.
notes: chappe behaviour: heartbeat_interval_ms should match the node's event-heartbeat-interval

text: Every probe interval the node runs its probe commands; an -ERR answer or no answer within the probe timeout marks it down and closes the connection.
notes: chappe behaviour: probes default to status, show calls count and sofia status; status and show calls count feed the load

text: Reconnect attempts back off exponentially with jitter between a minimum and a maximum wait, and the backoff resets once the node is up.
notes: chappe behaviour: wait N is a random point in the upper half of backoff_min_ms * 2^(N-1), capped at backoff_max_ms

text: Subscribers of a node, or of all nodes, receive its up, down, draining and load notices, and event subscribers its events.
notes: chappe behaviour: {chappe_esl_node, Name, up | down | draining | {load, Map} | {event, Event}} through pg

text: Nodes are added at runtime or from the application environment; invalid options are refused; without nodes the registry does not run.
notes: chappe behaviour: {error, {missing_option, host}} and {error, {bad_option, K}}; the nodes env starts the registry with the app

text: Selection returns a node that is up, not draining, not full and carries every requested tag, by fewest sessions, most idle CPU or weight; none_up when there is none.
notes: chappe behaviour: full is the lower of the configured max_sessions and the reported Max-Sessions; weight 0 is never picked by weighted

text: A drained node stays connected and usable for commands but is not selected until resumed.
notes: chappe behaviour: node_drain/1 shows draining, node_resume/1 shows up again

text: api and bgapi run on the node's own connection; a node that is not up answers down.
notes: chappe behaviour: node_api/2, node_bgapi/2; the BACKGROUND_JOB result reaches event subscribers

text: A call process becomes the connection's controlling process and receives its channel's events: myevents on an outbound connection, a Unique-ID filter and every event on an inbound one.
notes: chappe behaviour: chappe_esl_call:start/2; an inbound connection without a uuid is refused with {error, {missing_option, uuid}}

text: A sendmsg execute with an Event-UUID header is reported back as the Application-UUID of its CHANNEL_EXECUTE_COMPLETE; the client matches each completion to its own request, whatever the order.
notes: chappe behaviour: exec/5 and exec/3,4 wait with a timeout ({error, timeout}); other messages stay in the mailbox; wait => false returns the Application-UUID; a timed out application is stopped with uuid_break (when it starts, if queued) and its completion dropped

text: When execute-app-arg is absent, a text/plain sendmsg body is the application argument.
notes: chappe behaviour: an argument over 1024 bytes or with a line break travels in the body

text: Typed helpers run the matching dialplan application or api command with FreeSWITCH's argument order; play_and_get_digits returns the digits variable of its completion event.
notes: chappe behaviour: answer, playback, play_and_get_digits, record, record_session and its stop, send_dtmf, set, export, hangup, conference, uuid_audio_fork start and stop; arguments with spaces, quotes or backslashes are single quoted and escaped where FreeSWITCH splits on spaces

text: The owner receives DTMF digits, the hangup cause, completions no request waits for, the other channel events, and closed when the connection goes; requests in flight end with hangup or closed.
notes: chappe behaviour: {chappe_esl_call, Call, {dtmf, D} | {hangup, Cause} | {complete, App, Ev} | {event, Ev} | closed}

text: When the owner dies before the hangup, the call stops the audio forks and session recordings it started, then kills the channel, then closes the connection.
notes: chappe behaviour: uuid_audio_fork stop, uuid_record stop, uuid_kill; nothing is sent after the hangup or after stop/1
